title: Ivo and the Ember
premise: Marguerite Blackwood has spent seven years hiding among the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, believing her hedge-witch mistress sent her away for her own safety. When a dying courier presses a scorched map into her hands, she learns she is the last heir of the Emberwrights, the family who once forged the covenant binding the human realm to the fading Otherworld—and that the covenant's failure is why her mistress vanished. Hunted by a guild faction that profits from the breach and guided by Ivo, a shapeshifting ember-spirit bound to her bloodline, Marguerite must reach the Cinderforge before the autumn equinox and reforge the covenant with a sacrifice only an heir can make. In the end she refuses the old terms: instead of giving up her life or her belonging, she rewrites the covenant itself, sharing the burden between realms—and chooses to stay in both worlds at once, with Ivo at her side.
about_author: Kestrel Crane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trade ledgers from defunct merchant guilds, an obsession that bleeds into every page of their fiction. They write quiet, ledger-precise fantasy about people who inherit burdens they never asked for.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She balances impossible accounts by candlelight, invisible and safe, until a bleeding stranger collapses into the guildhall's counting room and dies pressing a scorched map into her hands. The beat: the fragile comfort of anonymity shattering in a single night.

chapters.title: What the Map Refuses to Say
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The map resists every attempt to read it—until her blood touches the parchment and it blooms with roads that shouldn't exist. Guildmaster Corvane notices her shaking hands. The beat: dread mixed with a shameful thrill of being seen.

chapters.title: Ivo
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Following the map's first road, she is ambushed by guild enforcers and saved by a fox made of banked fire who speaks her family name: Ivo, the Emberwrights' bound spirit, awake after thirty years. The beat: wonder, and the first taste of what inheritance truly costs.

chapters.title: The Mistress Who Lied
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He leads her toward the Cinderforge and reveals her mistress didn't send her away to protect her—she stole her as a child to keep the covenant unreforged. Marguerite's whole history curdles. The beat: grief for a childhood built on a lie.

chapters.title: Saltmarket
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In a border town where humans and Otherfolk trade uneasily, she witnesses what the broken covenant has done: dying orchards, changelings turned away, a market half-empty. She also finds allies—a ferrywoman, a moth-winged scribe. The beat: anger hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Corvane corners her with an offer: surrender the map and he'll let the Otherworld fade gently, sparing the human realm the war. He reveals the guild profited from the breach for decades. The beat: temptation—the old life offered back at a terrible price.

chapters.title: The Ferry at Duskwater
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Crossing into the Otherworld, they are pursued; the ferrywoman holds the enforcers off and drowns doing it. Ivo confesses he failed the last Emberwright—Marguerite's mother—at this same crossing. The beat: guilt shared, trust sealed in loss.

chapters.title: The Cinderforge
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the forge she learns the covenant's true terms: reforging demands an heir's life, freely given. Her mother died here refusing—or so the forge-wardens claim. With equinox hours away, Marguerite must decide whether any inheritance is worth her life. The beat: despair at the bottom of the arc.

chapters.title: Equinox
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Corvane's forces storm the forge as Marguerite takes up the hammer—but instead of the old sacrifice, she writes new terms into the burning metal: the burden split between both realms, renewed each year by shared tending rather than one death. Ivo feeds the forge his own ember-core to light it. The beat: defiant love against duty, climax and near-loss entwined.

chapters.title: A Ledger Rewritten
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The covenant holds; Ivo survives, diminished but hers, no longer bound but choosing to stay. Marguerite returns not to hiding but to the guildhall, where she begins a new ledger—one that records debts owed between worlds, and how they're paid. The beat: belonging claimed on her own terms, an ending that is also a beginning.
